objective: Design reward, observation/command, and retention checks that address lane drift before proposing more PPO updates.
reason: Update1 preserves binary outcomes but increases common-window lateral RMS by 15.23%; update2 improves stairs while introducing five friction failures. Scalar reward and aggregate completion alone miss these changes.
scope: Offline analysis and a reviewable design only.
input_recordings: fixed low LR update1 full first episodes
fixed low LR update2 full first episodes
steps: Compare active Source reward terms and actor observations with the reference project; document frames, units, weights, dt scaling, and terrain-height differences.

Use the saved common first-episode windows to quantify heading/lateral drift and rank illustrative successful, failed and earlier-failed episodes. Treat reconstructed scanner clearance as geometric evidence, not exact termination branch provenance.

Compare reward-only shaping, lane-feedback velocity/yaw commands with the existing 45-dimensional actor, and explicit observation augmentation. State observability and checkpoint-compatibility limits and recommend one bounded route.
Write candidate formulas, scales and configuration drafts; offline candidate scores must not be described as learned-policy improvement or a counterfactual simulator result.
Design future retention gates that keep current completion/safety/bounds criteria while adding per-condition lateral/heading metrics and checks for earlier endings on pre-existing failures.
Deliver a reviewable design and a separately budgeted proposed implementation/experiment; seek consent again before applying it.
compute: CPU-only offline scripts; each analysis command bounded to 120 seconds; no simulator or GPU workload.
acceptance_criteria: All 17 active reward terms and actual 45 actor inputs have documented reference mappings or explained differences.
Drift metrics reproduce from archived arrays with explicit windows, units, sample counts and exclusions.
The five new friction failures and three pre-existing stair failures are included; aggregate averages cannot hide per-condition tradeoffs.
One recommended design states required state, network/checkpoint compatibility, fallback/stop conditions, and limitations of offline scoring.
Future numeric evaluation thresholds and resource caps are proposed in writing before any implementation or simulation.
